title: Rock Stars Celebrate a Music School for Kids
summary:
On Saturday, famous rock bands played a big concert in Los Angeles. It was a party for the Silverlake Conservatory of Music, a music school for kids. The school turned 25 years old. The concert also raised money for the school.

Flea, the bass player of Red Hot Chili Peppers, helped start the school in 2001. Today it teaches music to 1,000 students each week. More than 200 students whose families cannot pay get free lessons and instruments.

Students played first! A student band called the SCM All Stars performed, and so did a student brass band. It was Flea's birthday weekend, so he got a birthday cake on stage.

Then Dave Grohl sang "My Hero," and his band, Foo Fighters, surprised everyone by joining him. Red Hot Chili Peppers played last.

Anahit, a student who started lessons at age 6, said music "brings such a good community."
why_it_matters: It helps more kids learn to play music, even if their families cannot pay for lessons.
